Coordinate transformations as materials — a cloak and a field rotator

Maxwell's equations are covariant under general coordinates. After a coordinate transformation of the plane, the equations that were vacuum in the transformed space take, on the original Cartesian grid, the form of the equations in an anisotropic material (transformation optics). Using this correspondence, a cloak that hides a conducting cylinder and a rotator that turns the wavefronts inside it by a fixed angle are computed on an ordinary Yee grid (electric and magnetic fields staggered by half a cell).

Top left: the reference pulse in vacuum. Top right: a bare conducting cylinder (shadow and reflection). Bottom left: a truncated cloak (map r′ = R2 (r − R1′)/(R2 − R1′)). Bottom right: a quarter-turn rotator (map φ′ = φ + f(r)). Color is the out-of-plane field Ez. Actual simulation data at wavelength 2 on a 320×240 grid (40 cells per wavelength). Scattering ratio and energy over time · Video file
∂tEz = εz−1(∂xHy − ∂yHx), ∂tB = −∇×E, Hi = (μ−1)ijBj
μij = √g gij, εz = √g, (μ−1)ij = gij/√g
g is the metric pulled back by the coordinate map. In the orthonormal polar frame (r̂, φ̂) the rotator has g = [[1+s², s], [s, 1]] (s = r f′(r), det g = 1) and the cloak has g = diag(h′², (r′/r)²) (h′ = R2/(R2 − R1′)); the program derives them from the maps instead of writing them.

The program states the coordinate map itself and Egison derives the material tensor: ∂/∂ differentiates the rotator map into its Jacobian, and a contraction in index notation turns it into the pulled-back metric: rotatedJacobian = withSymbols [k, i] (∂/∂ (rotated 0)~k coordinates~i), rotatedMetric = withSymbols [i, j, k] ((rotatedJacobian 0)~k_i . (rotatedJacobian 0)_k_j). The only line written by hand is the volume element √g (1 for the rotator, h′r′/r for the cloak). On the Yee grid Hx and By live at different points, so resample brings them to the same point before the contraction. The vacuum reference solution is advanced in the same program, and the ratio of scattered to incident field energy outside the device is integrated inside the generated solver. With the electric field on the dual grid and the magnetic field on the primal grid, one update reads two cells forward and one cell backward; Formura sizes the halo by this forward reach, so temporal blocking and MPI decomposition reproduce the single-process result.

Full Formurae source (transformation_optics.fme, 137 lines) 
-- Transformation optics: TE Maxwell (Ez, Bx, By) on a Cartesian Yee grid.
-- A coordinate map of the plane is realized as an anisotropic material with
-- mu^{ij} = sqrt(g) g^{ij} and eps_z = sqrt(g), where g is the metric of the
-- map pulled back to the physical plane (Ward and Pendry).  The map is the
-- only input: Egison differentiates it into the Jacobian, contracts the
-- Jacobian into the pulled-back metric and divides by the volume element,
-- all in index notation.  The vacuum reference (Ev, Bv) runs in the same program
-- so the scattered field is measured inside the generated solver.
-- z is a dummy periodic axis that carries the Yee (edge/face) placements.
-- E lives on the dual grid and B, H on the primal grid: H = mu^{-1} B
-- interpolates the new B to the other edge, B' reads E' one cell back and
-- E' reads H one cell ahead, so an update reaches two cells forward and one
-- cell backward.  Formura sizes the halo by the forward reach, which is why
-- this placement (and not the mirrored one) blocks and decomposes exactly.
-- H is kept as a field so that the E update does not go through the interpolation.
dimension 3
axes x, y, z
metric g

param dt = 0.1 * dx
param x0 = 3.0
-- the device centre sits a quarter cell off the nodes, edges and cell centres, so no
-- sample of the frame vectors or of 1/eps_z falls on the singular point r = 0
param cx = 8.0 + 0.25 * dx
param cy = 6.0 + 0.25 * dy
param width = 3.0
param wavenumber = 3.141592653589793
param R1 = 1.0
param R2 = 2.0
param R1s = 0.9
param twist = 0.7853981633974483
param cloak = 0.0
param rotator = 0.0
param obstacle = 0.0
param cell = dx * dy
extern sqrt
extern exp

-- The shifted coordinates are quoted (backquote) so that the CAS keeps them as
-- atoms: expanding (x - cx)^2 + (y - cy)^2 inside every root and product would
-- make the differentiation of the maps below take minutes instead of seconds.
def u unused = `(x - cx)
def v unused = `(y - cy)
def rr unused = sqrt ((u 0)^2 + (v 0)^2)
def shell unused = if rr 0 > R1 && rr 0 < R2 then 1 else 0
def core unused = if rr 0 < R1 then 1 else 0
-- The solver uses H = mu^{-1} B with mu^{-1}_{ij} = g_{ij} / sqrt(g).  Each map
-- sends a physical point to its image in the virtual (vacuum) plane; it is the
-- identity outside the shell R1 < r < R2 and is only used inside it.
-- rotator: (r, phi) -> (r, phi + twist (R2 - r)/(R2 - R1)), a rotation by an angle
-- that decreases from twist at R1 to zero at R2 (det g = 1, eps_z = 1).
def angle unused = twist * (R2 - rr 0) / (R2 - R1)
def rotated unused = [| cx + u 0 * cos (angle 0) - v 0 * sin (angle 0), cy + u 0 * sin (angle 0) + v 0 * cos (angle 0), z |]
-- cloak: r -> r' = R2 (r - R1s)/(R2 - R1s) with phi unchanged (R1s < R1 keeps every
-- value finite); sqrt(g) = h' r'/r with h' = R2/(R2 - R1s).
def stretch unused = R2 / (R2 - R1s)
def image unused = stretch 0 * (rr 0 - R1s)
def stretched unused = [| cx + image 0 * u 0 / rr 0, cy + image 0 * v 0 / rr 0, z |]
-- the Jacobian J^k_i of each map and its pulled-back metric g_ij = J^k_i J^k_j;
-- the two maps are differentiated separately so that no product of their terms
-- appears (the flags rotator and cloak are symbols during normalization)
def rotatedJacobian unused = withSymbols [k, i] (∂/∂ (rotated 0)~k coordinates~i)
def rotatedMetric unused = withSymbols [i, j, k] ((rotatedJacobian 0)~k_i . (rotatedJacobian 0)_k_j)
def stretchedJacobian unused = withSymbols [k, i] (∂/∂ (stretched 0)~k coordinates~i)
def stretchedMetric unused = withSymbols [i, j, k] ((stretchedJacobian 0)~k_i . (stretchedJacobian 0)_k_j)
-- sqrt(det g): 1 for the rotator and h' r'/r for the cloak.  This is the one line
-- written by hand: det g is the square of h' r'/r, but the CAS does not take the
-- root of a perfect square that contains a square root itself.
def volumeElement unused = 1 + cloak * (stretch 0 * image 0 / rr 0 - 1)
def permittivity unused = 1 + shell 0 * (volumeElement 0 - 1)
def inversePermittivity unused = (1 - core 0 * obstacle) / permittivity 0
-- mu^{-1}_ij = g_ij / sqrt(g) inside the shell and the identity g^{ij} elsewhere,
-- one tensor per device; the device is selected in the step by the flags so
-- that the two maps never meet in one expression during normalization
def rotatorMaterial unused = withSymbols [i, j] (shell 0 * (rotatedMetric 0)~i~j + (1 - shell 0) * g~i~j)
def cloakMaterial unused = withSymbols [i, j] (shell 0 * (stretchedMetric 0)~i~j / volumeElement 0 + (1 - shell 0) * g~i~j)
def pulse unused = exp (0 - ((x - x0) / width)^2) * cos (wavenumber * (x - x0))
-- the tail of the pulse must not be frozen inside the conductor, where E_z is held at zero
def masked unused = (1 - core 0 * obstacle) * pulse 0
-- The material tensors are frozen into fields at init (they never change in
-- time); the step selects the device, resamples mu^{-1} to the placement of
-- each H component and contracts it with B.
def hx M~a~b V_c = withSymbols [j] (M~1~j . V_j)
def hy M~a~b V_c = withSymbols [j] (M~2~j . V_j)
def curlz H_c = ∂_x H_2 - ∂_y H_1
def ez V_c = V_3
def magnetic V_c W_d = withSymbols [i, j] (g~i~j . V_i . W_j)

field E_i @ dual
field B_i @ primal
field H_i @ primal
field Ev_i @ dual
field Bv_i @ primal
field Mrot{~i~j} @ collocated
field Mcloak{~i~j} @ collocated
field epsz : scalar @ collocated
-- 1/eps_z sampled where E_z lives (the third component of a dual vector), so the
-- conductor mask stays sharp instead of being interpolated from the nodes
field ie_i @ dual
field outside : scalar @ collocated
field scatter : scalar @ collocated
field incident : scalar @ collocated
field energy : scalar @ collocated

init:
  E_i := [| 0, 0, masked 0 |]_i
  B_i := [| 0, 0 - masked 0, 0 |]_i
  H_i := [| 0, 0 - masked 0, 0 |]_i
  Ev_i := [| 0, 0, pulse 0 |]_i
  Bv_i := [| 0, 0 - pulse 0, 0 |]_i
  Mrot~i~j := rotatorMaterial 0
  Mcloak~i~j := cloakMaterial 0
  epsz := permittivity 0
  ie_i := [| 0, 0, inversePermittivity 0 |]_i
  outside := if rr 0 > R2 + 0.5 then cell else 0
  scatter := 0
  incident := 0
  energy := 0

step:
  local Minv{~i~j} @ collocated = rotator * Mrot~i~j + cloak * Mcloak~i~j + (1 - rotator - cloak) * g~i~j
  E'_i = [| 0, 0, E_3 + dt * ie_3 * curlz H |]_i
  B' = B - dt * curl E'
  H'_i = [| hx (resample(Minv, 1, 0, 0)) (resample(B', 1, 0, 0)), hy (resample(Minv, 0, 1, 0)) (resample(B', 0, 1, 0)), 0 |]_i
  Ev' = Ev + dt * curl Bv
  Bv' = Bv - dt * curl Ev'
  Mrot' = Mrot
  Mcloak' = Mcloak
  epsz' = epsz
  ie' = ie
  outside' = outside
  -- the difference is formed before squaring, so that the vacuum case measures the
  -- actual departure from the reference copy rather than cancellation error
  local diff @ collocated = ez (resample(E', 0, 0, 0)) - ez (resample(Ev', 0, 0, 0))
  scatter' = outside * diff^2
  incident' = outside * (ez (resample(Ev', 0, 0, 0)))^2
  energy' = cell * (epsz * (ez (resample(E', 0, 0, 0)))^2 + magnetic (resample(B', 0, 0, 0)) (resample(H', 0, 0, 0))) / 2

def FormuraeInternalEncodeTensor expectedShape variances degree value :=
  let actualVariances := Formurae.logicalTensorVariances value
      actualDegree := dfOrder value
      exactMetadata := actualVariances = variances && actualDegree = degree
      completesOmittedDownIndices := degree = 0
                                      && actualDegree > 0
                                      && actualVariances = variances
   in match assert "normalized equation tensor metadata mismatch"
                   (tensorShape value = expectedShape
                    && (exactMetadata || completesOmittedDownIndices)) as bool with
        | #True -> FEIR.encodeTensorWithMetadata feParameters feCoordinatesRegistry feFields feIntrinsics feAnalytics variances degree value

At t = 10 the scattering ratio ∫(Ez − Ezvac)²dA / ∫(Ezvac)²dA outside the device (r > R2 + 0.5) is below 10−32 in vacuum (machine precision), 0.44 for the bare cylinder, 0.15 for the cloak and 0.009 for the rotator. The electromagnetic energy stays constant within 0.2% in all four cases. A half-turn rotator makes the material extremely anisotropic (eigenvalue ratio above 100) and leaves a residual scattering of 0.18 at this resolution, which is why the default is a quarter turn.
Regenerate: make transformation_optics-demo → python examples/transformation_optics/render.py --video. Additional checks: make transformation_optics-verify (zero scattering in vacuum, energy conservation, the scattering ratios of the devices, resolution dependence, agreement with temporal blocking and MPI). Elastic waves in a spherical shell with walls — one program for spherical and non-orthogonal coordinates

Linear elastic waves (velocity and stress) in the band of a spherical shell between the spheres R = 1 and R = 2 and the cones of colatitude arctan 2 and π − arctan 2 around the equator. Every wall is rigid (the velocity is held at zero) and the longitude is periodic. The same program runs in spherical coordinates and in non-orthogonal coordinates of the same shell, a chart whose longitude winds with the radius, declared by its metric tensor. With λ = 2 and μ = ρ0 = 1 the P wave (compression) travels at speed 2 and the S wave (shear) at speed 1, so a localized velocity pulse along the longitude separates into two shells; the S wave reflects at the walls while the P wave runs around the shell.

The equatorial plane through the source on a 97×65×256 grid (radial nodes, colatitude nodes, longitude cells). Red is the P indicator a|∇·v|/V0, blue the S indicator a|∇×v|/V0 (square-root color scale up to 0.2 and 0.5). Black circles are the walls R = 1 and R = 2, dashed circles have radii cPt and cSt, and thin lines are every 16th grid line drawn at their physical positions, so the longitude lines of the bottom row wind with the radius. The third column adds one term αninjnknlekl (α = 3, n along the radius) to the constitutive function.
eij = ½(gik∂jvk + gjk∂ivk + (∂kgij)vk),  ∇jσij = (gik/J)∂j(Jgklσlj) − ½gik(∂kgjl)σjl,  ∂tσij = Cijklekl,  Cijkl = λgijgkl + μ(gikgjl + gilgjk)
The coordinates are the radius r, the colatitude θ, and φ, mapped to the longitude Φ = φ + s(r − 1) (an origin declaration makes r and θ the radius and the colatitude themselves). The metric is [[1 + (s r sin θ)², 0, s r² sin²θ], [0, r², 0], [s r² sin²θ, 0, r² sin²θ]] with √det g = r² sin θ; only the parameter twist = s changes between the two coordinate systems.

The three operators use the metric g_i_j, its inverse g~i~j, the volume element volume, and the analytic derivative ∂/∂ g_i_j coordinates~k in place; Egison expands and simplifies them when the program is compiled, and the generated time step evaluates the surviving coefficients from the cell coordinates (no array stores the metric). boundary r : sbp and boundary θ : sbp request summation-by-parts differences on the bounded axes, and the constants the declaration supplies (sbpLoR and the like) mask the velocity on the wall nodes; the force is masked before it moves the velocity, so one step is a symplectic map of the interior state. Every quantity of the evaluation is a field of the program: the two wave indicators, the elastic energy and the modified energy that velocity Verlet preserves, the outer radius of each shell (a max reduction of the distance where the indicator exceeds 0.01), and the error against the exact torsional mode (order-3 spherical Bessel profile, angular part P31). The driver only starts the solver and writes records; render.py maps the saved equatorial slices to physical positions.

Full Formurae source (elastic_shell.fme, 126 lines) 
-- Linear elastic waves (velocity-stress form) in a spherical shell with
-- rigid walls, written once for a family of coordinate systems.  The
-- coordinates are the radius r (from 1 to 2), the colatitude θ (from
-- arctan 2 to π - arctan 2, the band around the equator), and φ, which is
-- mapped to the longitude Φ = φ + twist * (r - 1): twist = 0 is spherical
-- coordinates, twist > 0 a non-orthogonal chart of the same shell whose
-- longitude lines wind with the radius.  The walls are coordinate surfaces
-- in every chart: the velocity vanishes on the spheres r = 1 and r = 2 and
-- on the two cones, and φ stays periodic.
--
-- The metric of the map is declared by its components.  The operators use
-- the metric, its inverse, and its analytic derivatives in place: Egison
-- differentiates and simplifies them at compile time, and the generated
-- time step evaluates the resulting coefficients from the cell coordinates.
-- With lambda = 2, mu = rho0 = 1 the P-wave speed is 2 and the S-wave
-- speed is 1.
dimension 3
axes r, θ, φ
origin r = 1.0
origin θ = 1.1071487177940906
metric g
metric tensor [[1 + (twist * r * sin θ)^2, 0, twist * (r * sin θ)^2], [0, r^2, 0], [twist * (r * sin θ)^2, 0, (r * sin θ)^2]]
metric volume r^2 * sin θ

boundary r : sbp
boundary θ : sbp

param λ = 2.0
param μ = 1.0
param ρ0 = 1.0
param dt = 0.05 * dr
param twist = 0.0
param radius = 0.25
param x0 = -1.5
param y0 = 0.0
param z0 = 0.0
param cell = dr * dθ * dφ
param front = 0.0001
extern exp
extern sqrt

-- physical position of a cell, and its physical distance from the source
-- (radius 1.5, colatitude pi/2, longitude pi)
def longitude unused = φ + twist * (r - 1)
def distance2 unused = (r * sin θ * cos (longitude 0) - x0)^2 + (r * sin θ * sin (longitude 0) - y0)^2 + (r * cos θ - z0)^2
-- the exponent is selected first, so that no overflowing value is formed;
-- the support stops at 0.995 radius (f < 1e-86 there), which keeps the
-- denominator positive under rounding of the expanded polynomials
def bump unused = if distance2 0 < 0.99 * radius^2 then 0 - 2 * distance2 0 / (radius^2 - distance2 0) else 0
def pulse unused = if distance2 0 < 0.99 * radius^2 then exp (bump 0) else 0
-- the expanded sums of squares can round to a small negative number, so the
-- square roots below are guarded
def distance unused = if distance2 0 < 0 then 0 else sqrt (distance2 0)
-- the summation-by-parts weight of a node: half on a wall
def weight unused = (if r < sbpLoR || r > sbpHiR then 0.5 else 1) * (if θ < sbpLoTheta || θ > sbpHiTheta then 0.5 else 1)
def strain V~a = withSymbols [i, j, k] ((g_i_k . ∂_j V~k + g_j_k . ∂_i V~k + (∂/∂ g_i_j coordinates~k) . V~k) / 2)
def stressRate E_i_j = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] (λ * g~i~j * (g~k~l . E_k_l) + 2 * μ * (g~i~k . g~j~l . E_k_l))
def stressDiv S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] ((g~i~k . ∂_j (volume * (g_k_l . S~l~j))) / volume - (g~i~k . (∂/∂ g_j_l coordinates~k) . S~j~l) / 2)
-- coordinate-independent diagnostics of a velocity field
def waveDiv V~a = withSymbols [i] ((∂_i (volume * V~i)) / volume)
def waveCurl V~a = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] ((epsilon~i~j~k . ∂_j (g_k_l . V~l)) / volume)
def norm2 W~a = withSymbols [i, j] (g_i_j . W~i . W~j)
def stressNorm S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] (g_i_k . g_j_l . S~i~j . S~k~l)
def stressTrace S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j] (g_i_j . S~i~j)

field v~i @ collocated
field σ{~i~j} @ collocated
field compression : scalar @ collocated
field shearing : scalar @ collocated
field energy : scalar @ collocated
field modified : scalar @ collocated
field pw : scalar @ collocated
field pr : scalar @ collocated
field sw : scalar @ collocated
field sr : scalar @ collocated
field pfront : scalar @ collocated
field sfront : scalar @ collocated

init:
  v~i := [| 0, 0, pulse 0 / (r * sin θ) |]~i
  σ~i~j := [| [| 0, 0, 0 |], [| 0, 0, 0 |], [| 0, 0, 0 |] |]~i~j
  compression := 0
  shearing := 0
  energy := 0
  modified := 0
  pw := 0
  pr := 0
  sw := 0
  sr := 0
  pfront := 0
  sfront := 0

step:
  -- velocity Verlet: half velocity, full stress, half velocity; the mask
  -- clamps the velocity on the wall nodes of both bounded axes, which keeps
  -- the step a symplectic map of the interior state
  let wall = (if r < sbpLoR || r > sbpHiR then 0 else 1) * (if θ < sbpLoTheta || θ > sbpHiTheta then 0 else 1)
  let vm~i = [| wall, wall, wall |]~i
  local force~i @ collocated = stressDiv σ
  -- the force the step applies: zero on the walls
  local kick~i @ collocated = vm~i * force~i
  local half~i @ collocated = vm~i * v~i + (dt / (2 * ρ0)) * kick~i
  local strainRate{_i_j} @ collocated = strain half
  local rate{~i~j} @ collocated = stressRate strainRate
  σ'~i~j = σ~i~j + dt * rate~i~j
  local nextForce~i @ collocated = stressDiv σ'
  v'~i = vm~i * (half~i + (dt / (2 * ρ0)) * nextForce~i)
  -- diagnostics of the state entering the step: P-wave indicator (divergence),
  -- S-wave indicator (norm of the curl), elastic energy, the energy that the
  -- Verlet step preserves, the moments of the P and S shells, and the physical
  -- distance from the source of the farthest point where the dimensionless
  -- indicator exceeds sqrt(front) (the outer edge of each shell, which
  -- advances at the wave speed)
  local far @ collocated = distance 0
  compression' = waveDiv v
  local curlv~i @ collocated = waveCurl v
  local curl2 @ collocated = norm2 curlv
  shearing' = if curl2 < 0 then 0 else sqrt curl2
  energy' = weight 0 * cell * volume * (ρ0 * norm2 v / 2 + stressNorm σ / (4 * μ) - λ * (stressTrace σ)^2 / (4 * μ * (3 * λ + 2 * μ)))
  modified' = energy' - weight 0 * cell * volume * dt^2 * norm2 kick / (8 * ρ0)
  pw' = weight 0 * cell * volume * compression'^2
  pr' = pw' * far
  sw' = weight 0 * cell * volume * shearing'^2
  sr' = sw' * far
  pfront' = if radius^2 * compression'^2 > front then far else 0
  sfront' = if radius^2 * shearing'^2 > front then far else 0

Temporal blocking (interval 4) and MPI decompositions across the walls (three processes along the radius, six with the longitude split as well) reproduce the plain build with zero difference in both coordinate systems; the generated Formura sources of the two coordinate systems differ only in the line double :: twist. The exact torsional mode converges at orders 1.97, 1.99 (N = 16, 32, 64) in both coordinate systems (the mode is axisymmetric and the second chart only shears the longitude, so the errors coincide to rounding). On a shell of thickness 2 (radius 1 to 3, source at radius 2), where the speeds can be measured before any front meets a wall, the outer radii of the P and S shells grow at 1.93 and 1.07 (spherical) and 1.90 and 1.06 (non-orthogonal) against the exact 2 and 1 (the fixed threshold follows the edge of the discrete front), the two coordinate systems agree within 0.021 in the outer radii (longitude spacing 0.074 at the outer wall), 0.008 in the mean radii, and 10−7 in energy, and the modified energy drifts by 8×10−14 over 512 steps. In the demonstration runs behind the figure (97×65×256 grid, 1536 steps, ten processes) the energy stays within [0.999993, 1], the modified energy drifts by less than 10−14, the two coordinate systems agree within 0.017 in the outer radii, 0.001 in the mean radii, and 6×10−6 in energy, and their speed fields on the equatorial plane differ by 7% in relative L² at t = 0.4 (compared at the same physical points; the indicator fields, which are derivatives, by about 20%).
Regenerate: make elastic_shell-demo → python3 examples/elastic_shell/render.py. Additional checks: make elastic_shell-verify (blocking/MPI reproduction, parameter independence of the generated source, mode convergence, energy, front speeds, agreement of the two coordinate systems). Description and run instructions (Japanese) · Verification data and execution environment · Demonstration runs

Elastic waves in a periodic box — one program for Cartesian and non-orthogonal coordinates

Linear elastic waves (velocity and stress) on a periodic cube of side 4. The same program runs in Cartesian coordinates and in non-orthogonal coordinates of the same cube, a chart whose grid lines wave sideways, declared by its metric tensor. With λ = 2 and μ = ρ0 = 1 the P wave (compression) travels at speed 2 and the S wave (shear) at speed 1, so a localized velocity pulse separates into two shells whose radii grow as 2t and t.

The plane through the source on a 128³ grid. Red is the P indicator a|∇·v|/V0, blue the S indicator a|∇×v|/V0 (square-root color scale up to 0.2 and 0.5). Dashed circles have radii cPt and cSt; thin lines are every 16th grid line, drawn at their physical positions, so the bottom row shows the same waves over a wavy grid. The third column adds one term αninjnknlekl (α = 3, n = (1,1,0)/√2) to the constitutive function and stretches both fronts along n.
eij = ½(gik∂jvk + gjk∂ivk + (∂kgij)vk),  ∇jσij = (gik/J)∂j(Jgklσlj) − ½gik(∂kgjl)σjl,  ∂tσij = Cijklekl,  Cijkl = λgijgkl + μ(gikgjl + gilgjk)
Coordinates (x, y, z) are mapped to (x + s sin(2πy/L), y, z); the metric is [[1, c, 0], [c, 1+c², 0], [0, 0, 1]] with c = s(2π/L)cos(2πy/L) and det g = 1. Only the parameter shear = s changes between the two coordinate systems.

The three operators use the metric g_i_j, its inverse g~i~j, the volume element volume, and the analytic derivative ∂/∂ g_i_j coordinates~k in place. Egison expands and simplifies them when the program is compiled, and the generated time step evaluates the surviving coefficients from the cell coordinates (no array stores the metric). Temporal blocking and a two-process MPI decomposition reproduce the plain build exactly (Formura's code generator, which computed the coordinates inside a blocked step wrongly, is fixed in our fork). Every quantity of the evaluation is a field of the program: the two wave indicators, the elastic energy and the modified energy that velocity Verlet preserves, the outer radius of each shell (a max reduction of the distance where the indicator exceeds 0.01), and the errors against exact plane P and S waves. The driver only starts the solver and writes records; render.py maps the saved slices to physical positions.

Full Formurae source (elastic_pulse.fme, 105 lines) 
-- Linear elastic waves (velocity-stress form) in a periodic box, written once
-- for a family of coordinate systems.  The coordinates (x, y, z) are mapped to
-- physical positions (x + shear * sin (wavenumber * y), y, z): shear = 0 is
-- Cartesian coordinates, shear > 0 a non-orthogonal chart of the same box
-- whose grid lines wave sideways.  Both directions stay periodic.
--
-- The metric of the map is declared by its components.  The operators use
-- the metric, its inverse, and its analytic derivatives in place: Egison
-- differentiates and simplifies them at compile time, and the generated
-- time step evaluates the resulting coefficients from the cell coordinates.
-- With lambda = 2, mu = rho0 = 1 the P-wave speed is 2 and the S-wave
-- speed is 1.
dimension 3
axes x, y, z
metric g
metric tensor [[1, shear * wavenumber * cos (wavenumber * y), 0], [shear * wavenumber * cos (wavenumber * y), 1 + (shear * wavenumber * cos (wavenumber * y))^2, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
metric volume 1

param λ = 2.0
param μ = 1.0
param ρ0 = 1.0
param dt = 0.1 * dx
param shear = 0.0
param wavenumber = 1.5707963267948966
param radius = 0.25
param x0 = 2.0
param y0 = 2.0
param z0 = 2.0
param cell = dx * dy * dz
param front = 0.0001
extern exp
extern sqrt

-- physical position along x, and the physical distance from the source
def physical unused = x + shear * sin (wavenumber * y)
def distance2 unused = (physical 0 - x0)^2 + (y - y0)^2 + (z - z0)^2
-- the exponent is selected first, so that no overflowing value is formed;
-- the support stops at 0.995 radius (f < 1e-86 there), which keeps the
-- denominator positive under rounding of the expanded polynomials
def bump unused = if distance2 0 < 0.99 * radius^2 then 0 - 2 * distance2 0 / (radius^2 - distance2 0) else 0
def pulse unused = if distance2 0 < 0.99 * radius^2 then exp (bump 0) else 0
def strain V~a = withSymbols [i, j, k] ((g_i_k . ∂_j V~k + g_j_k . ∂_i V~k + (∂/∂ g_i_j coordinates~k) . V~k) / 2)
def stressRate E_i_j = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] (λ * g~i~j * (g~k~l . E_k_l) + 2 * μ * (g~i~k . g~j~l . E_k_l))
def stressDiv S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] ((g~i~k . ∂_j (volume * (g_k_l . S~l~j))) / volume - (g~i~k . (∂/∂ g_j_l coordinates~k) . S~j~l) / 2)
-- coordinate-independent diagnostics of a velocity field
def waveDiv V~a = withSymbols [i] ((∂_i (volume * V~i)) / volume)
def waveCurl V~a = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] ((epsilon~i~j~k . ∂_j (g_k_l . V~l)) / volume)
def norm2 W~a = withSymbols [i, j] (g_i_j . W~i . W~j)
def stressNorm S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j, k, l] (g_i_k . g_j_l . S~i~j . S~k~l)
def stressTrace S~a~b = withSymbols [i, j] (g_i_j . S~i~j)

field v~i @ collocated
field σ{~i~j} @ collocated
field compression : scalar @ collocated
field shearing : scalar @ collocated
field energy : scalar @ collocated
field modified : scalar @ collocated
field pw : scalar @ collocated
field pr : scalar @ collocated
field sw : scalar @ collocated
field sr : scalar @ collocated
field pfront : scalar @ collocated
field sfront : scalar @ collocated

init:
  v~i := [| pulse 0, 0, 0 |]~i
  σ~i~j := [| [| 0, 0, 0 |], [| 0, 0, 0 |], [| 0, 0, 0 |] |]~i~j
  compression := 0
  shearing := 0
  energy := 0
  modified := 0
  pw := 0
  pr := 0
  sw := 0
  sr := 0
  pfront := 0
  sfront := 0

step:
  -- velocity Verlet: half velocity, full stress, half velocity
  local force~i @ collocated = stressDiv σ
  local half~i @ collocated = v~i + (dt / (2 * ρ0)) * force~i
  local e{_i_j} @ collocated = strain half
  local rate{~i~j} @ collocated = stressRate e
  σ'~i~j = σ~i~j + dt * rate~i~j
  local nextForce~i @ collocated = stressDiv σ'

Temporal blocking and two-process MPI runs reproduce the plain build with zero difference in both coordinate systems; the generated Formura sources of the two coordinate systems differ only in the line double :: shear. Exact plane P and S waves converge at orders 1.95–1.99 (N = 16, 32, 64) in both coordinate systems. On the 128³ grid the outer radii of the P and S shells grow at 1.86 and 0.96 (Cartesian) and 1.86 and 0.95 (non-orthogonal) against the exact 2 and 1 (the pulse edge carries the shortest wavelengths, which centered differences propagate slowly), the two coordinate systems agree within 0.007 (grid spacing 0.031), and the modified energy drifts by 4×10−13 over 256 steps.
Regenerate: make elastic_pulse-demo → python3 examples/elastic_pulse/render.py. Additional checks: make elastic_pulse-verify (blocking/MPI reproduction, parameter independence of the generated source, plane-wave convergence, energy, front speeds, agreement of the two coordinate systems). Annulus in polar coordinates (flat)

Δu = (1/r)∂r(r∂ru) + (1/r²)∂φφu, r ∈ [1,2]  Curvature 0 — only the coordinates are curved
Full Formurae source (polar2d.fme, 22 lines) 
-- Heat equation on a PLANAR ANNULUS in polar coordinates
-- (r_phys, phi) = (1 + r, phi), r_phys in [1, 2].  The geometry is
-- flat (curvature 0) -- only the COORDINATES are curved: from the
-- embedding the CAS derives g = diag(1, (1+r)^2), i.e. the textbook
-- polar Laplacian (1/r) d_r (r d_r u) + (1/r^2) d_phiphi u, assembled
-- as an exactly conservative flux form.  The r walls are Neumann
-- (mirror), phi is periodic.

dimension 3
axes r, φ, z

param dt = 0.0001

embedding [ `(1 + r) * cos φ, `(1 + r) * sin φ, z ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := exp (0 - 4 * (r - 1 / 2) ^ 2) * exp (cos φ - 1)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u

dimension :: 3
axes :: r,phi,z

double :: dt = 0.0001

extern function :: cos
extern function :: exp

begin function (u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3) = init()
  double [] :: u, deltaCoeff_1, deltaCoeff_2, deltaCoeff_3
  u[i,j,k] = exp((-2) + (-4) * (dr * i)**2 + 4 * dr * i + cos(dphi * j))
  deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] = 1 + dr * ((1 / 2) + i)
  deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] = 1 / (1 + dr * i)
  deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] = 1 + dr * i
end function

begin function (u',deltaCoeff_1',deltaCoeff_2',deltaCoeff_3') = step(u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3)
  double [] :: u', deltaCoeff_1', deltaCoeff_2', deltaCoeff_3'
  deltaCoeff_1'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_2'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_3'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k]
  deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] * (u[i+1,j,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dr
  deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] * (u[i,j+1,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dphi
  deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] * (u[i,j,k+1] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dz
  u'[i,j,k] = (u[i,j,k] + dr * i * u[i,j,k] + dt * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dr + dt * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dphi + dt * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dz) / (1 + dr * i)
end function

-- Heat equation in FULL 3D SPHERICAL COORDINATES, on a shell:
-- (r_phys, theta_phys, phi) = (1 + r, 1 + theta, phi),
-- r_phys in [1, 2], theta_phys in [1, 1 + L] (poles avoided).
-- All three axes are nontrivial.  From the embedding the CAS derives
-- g = diag(1, (1+r)^2, (1+r)^2 sin^2(1+theta)) -- the spherical
-- Laplacian -- checks orthogonality symbolically, and assembles the
-- conservative flux form.  Both r and theta walls are Neumann
-- (mirror), phi is periodic.

dimension 3
axes r, θ, φ

param dt = 0.0002

embedding [ `(1 + r) * sin (1 + θ) * cos φ, `(1 + r) * sin (1 + θ) * sin φ, `(1 + r) * cos (1 + θ) ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := exp (0 - 4 * (r - 1 / 2) ^ 2) * exp (0 - 4 * (θ - 1 / 2) ^ 2) * exp (cos φ - 1)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u

begin function (u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3) = init()
  double [] :: u, deltaCoeff_1, deltaCoeff_2, deltaCoeff_3
  u[i,j,k] = exp((-3) + (-4) * (dr * i)**2 + (-4) * (dtheta * j)**2 + 4 * dr * i + 4 * dtheta * j + cos(dphi * k))
  deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] = 2 * dr * ((1 / 2) + i) * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + (dr * ((1 / 2) + i))**2 * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + sin(1 + dtheta * j)
  deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] = sin(1 + dtheta * ((1 / 2) + j))
  deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] = (2 * dr * i * sin(1 + dtheta * j)**(-1) + (dr * i)**2 * sin(1 + dtheta * j)**(-1) + sin(1 + dtheta * j)**(-1)) / (1 + 2 * dr * i + (dr * i)**2)
end function

begin function (u',deltaCoeff_1',deltaCoeff_2',deltaCoeff_3') = step(u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3)
  double [] :: u', deltaCoeff_1', deltaCoeff_2', deltaCoeff_3'
  deltaCoeff_1'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_2'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_3'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k]
  deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] * (u[i+1,j,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dr
  deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] * (u[i,j+1,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dtheta
  deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] * (u[i,j,k+1] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dphi
  u'[i,j,k] = (2 * dr * i * u[i,j,k] * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + dt * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dr + dt * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dtheta + dt * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dphi + u[i,j,k] * (dr * i)**2 * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + u[i,j,k] * sin(1 + dtheta * j)) / (2 * dr * i * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + (dr * i)**2 * sin(1 + dtheta * j) + sin(1 + dtheta * j))
end function

Full Formurae source (metric_torus.fme, 28 lines) 
-- Heat equation on a curved surface (a torus), from the COORDINATES:
-- the embedding of the (theta, phi, z) chart into R^4 below is the
-- only geometric input.  The compiler differentiates it (CAS), forms
-- the metric g_ab = dX/dx_a . dX/dx_b, checks orthogonality
-- symbolically (generation is gated on g_12 = g_13 = g_23 = 0),
-- takes the scale factors h_a = sqrt(g_aa), evaluates the hodge
-- factors sqrt(g)/h_a^2 at the half-cell placements, freezes them
-- into coefficient fields, and lowers the canonical scalar Δ to an
-- exactly conservative flux form.
--
-- Backquotes keep `(2 + cos θ) atomic during the CAS work
-- (sin^2 + cos^2 collapses to 1, sqrt of the quoted square reduces),
-- and quote-transparent substitution keeps the reduced factor compact.

dimension 3
axes θ, φ, z

param dt = 0.0005

embedding [ `(2 + cos θ) * cos φ, `(2 + cos θ) * sin φ, sin θ, z ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := exp (cos θ + cos φ - 2)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u

dimension :: 3
axes :: theta,phi,z

double :: dt = 0.0005

extern function :: cos
extern function :: exp

begin function (u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3) = init()
  double [] :: u, deltaCoeff_1, deltaCoeff_2, deltaCoeff_3
  u[i,j,k] = exp((-2) + cos(dphi * j) + cos(dtheta * i))
  deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] = 2 + cos(dtheta * ((1 / 2) + i))
  deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] = 1 / (2 + cos(dtheta * i))
  deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] = 2 + cos(dtheta * i)
end function

begin function (u',deltaCoeff_1',deltaCoeff_2',deltaCoeff_3') = step(u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3)
  double [] :: u', deltaCoeff_1', deltaCoeff_2', deltaCoeff_3'
  deltaCoeff_1'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_2'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_3'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k]
  deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] * (u[i+1,j,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dtheta
  deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] * (u[i,j+1,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dphi
  deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] * (u[i,j,k+1] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dz
  u'[i,j,k] = (2 * u[i,j,k] + dt * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dtheta + dt * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dphi + dt * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dz + u[i,j,k] * cos(dtheta * i)) / (2 + cos(dtheta * i))
end function
Time evolution of u (t=0 → 3000, shaded 3D) drawn on the torus
Matches an independent C reference to 3.3e-16 (all digits agree); metric-weighted heat Σ√g·u conserved to 2.5e-15; maximum principle holds. The scale-factor-derived .fmr is byte-identical to the hand-expanded version.

Band of the sphere (positive curvature)

∂tu = ΔS²u,  a band at colatitude θ ∈ [1, 1+L]
the CAS derives g=diag(1, sin²θ) from the embedding; the θ walls are mirror (Neumann)
Full Formurae source (metric_sphere.fme, 23 lines) 
-- Heat equation on a BAND OF THE UNIT SPHERE (positive curvature),
-- colatitude theta_phys = 1 + theta in [1, 1 + L] (poles avoided).
-- The embedding below is the only geometric input: the compiler
-- derives g = diag(1, sin^2(1+theta)) via the CAS (sin^2+cos^2
-- collapses, sqrt of the square closes), checks orthogonality, and
-- assembles the conservative Laplace-Beltrami flux form.  The theta
-- walls are Neumann (yaml boundary: mirror), so the metric-weighted
-- heat sum(sin(1+theta) u) is exactly conserved.

dimension 3
axes θ, φ, z

param dt = 0.0001

embedding [ sin (1 + θ) * cos φ, sin (1 + θ) * sin φ, cos (1 + θ), z ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := exp (0 - 4 * (θ - 1 / 2) ^ 2) * exp (cos φ - 1)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u

def FormuraeInternalEncodeTensor expectedShape variances degree value :=
  let actualVariances := Formurae.logicalTensorVariances value
      actualDegree := dfOrder value
      exactMetadata := actualVariances = variances && actualDegree = degree
      completesOmittedDownIndices := degree = 0
                                      && actualDegree > 0
                                      && actualVariances = variances
   in match assert "normalized equation tensor metadata mismatch"
                   (tensorShape value = expectedShape
                    && (exactMetadata || completesOmittedDownIndices)) as bool with
        | #True -> FEIR.encodeTensorWithMetadata feParameters feCoordinatesRegistry feFields feIntrinsics feAnalytics variances degree value

def FormuraeInternalEncodeTensorFromValue value :=

dimension :: 3
axes :: theta,phi,z

double :: dt = 0.0001

extern function :: sin
extern function :: cos
extern function :: exp

begin function (u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3) = init()
  double [] :: u, deltaCoeff_1, deltaCoeff_2, deltaCoeff_3
  u[i,j,k] = exp((-2) + (-4) * (dtheta * i)**2 + 4 * dtheta * i + cos(dphi * j))
  deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] = sin(1 + dtheta * ((1 / 2) + i))
  deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] = sin(1 + dtheta * i)**(-1)
  deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] = sin(1 + dtheta * i)
end function

begin function (u',deltaCoeff_1',deltaCoeff_2',deltaCoeff_3') = step(u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3)
  double [] :: u', deltaCoeff_1', deltaCoeff_2', deltaCoeff_3'
  deltaCoeff_1'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_2'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_3'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k]
  deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] * (u[i+1,j,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dtheta

end function

Full Formurae source (hyperbolic.fme, 23 lines) 
-- Heat equation on the POINCARE HALF-PLANE (constant NEGATIVE
-- curvature -1): ds^2 = (dx^2 + dy^2) / y_phys^2 with
-- y_phys = 1 + y in [1, 2].  A genuinely non-Euclidean geometry that
-- admits no embedding into R^3, so the metric is given directly by
-- its scale factors; the compiler derives sqrt(g) = 1/(1+y)^2 and the
-- hodge factors (both 1 -- the hyperbolic Laplacian is
-- (1+y)^2 (u_xx + u_yy)) and assembles the conservative flux form.
-- The y walls are Neumann (mirror), x is periodic.

dimension 3
axes x, y, z

param dt = 0.00002

metric scale [ 1 / (1 + y), 1 / (1 + y), 1 ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := exp (cos x - 1) * exp (0 - 4 * (y - 1 / 2) ^ 2)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u

dimension :: 3
axes :: x,y,z

double :: dt = 0.00002

extern function :: cos
extern function :: exp

begin function (u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3) = init()
  double [] :: u, deltaCoeff_1, deltaCoeff_2, deltaCoeff_3
  u[i,j,k] = exp((-2) + (-4) * (dy * j)**2 + 4 * dy * j + cos(dx * i))
  deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] = 1
  deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] = 1
  deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] = 1 / (1 + 2 * dy * j + (dy * j)**2)
end function

begin function (u',deltaCoeff_1',deltaCoeff_2',deltaCoeff_3') = step(u,deltaCoeff_1,deltaCoeff_2,deltaCoeff_3)
  double [] :: u', deltaCoeff_1', deltaCoeff_2', deltaCoeff_3'
  deltaCoeff_1'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_2'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k]
  deltaCoeff_3'[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k]
  deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_1[i,j,k] * (u[i+1,j,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dx
  deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_2[i,j,k] * (u[i,j+1,k] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dy
  deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] = deltaCoeff_3[i,j,k] * (u[i,j,k+1] + (-1) * u[i,j,k]) / dz
  u'[i,j,k] = u[i,j,k] + 2 * dt * dy * j * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dx + 2 * dt * dy * j * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dy + 2 * dt * dy * j * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dz + dt * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dx + dt * (deltaFlux_1[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_1[i-1,j,k]) / dx * (dy * j)**2 + dt * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dy + dt * (deltaFlux_2[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_2[i,j-1,k]) / dy * (dy * j)**2 + dt * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dz + dt * (deltaFlux_3[i,j,k] + (-1) * deltaFlux_3[i,j,k-1]) / dz * (dy * j)**2
end function
u on the half-plane chart (t=0 → 0.1): the effective diffusion y² is faster toward the top (large y)
Matches an independent reference implementation to 6.7e-16; Σu/y² conserved to 9.8e-16; maximum principle holds.

Yin-Yang overset — the full sphere (2 panels, 1 kernel)

∂tu = ΔS²u (Laplace–Beltrami on the unit sphere)
Full Formurae source (yinyang_diffusion.fme, 33 lines) 
-- Heat equation on ONE PANEL of the Yin-Yang overset grid for the
-- FULL unit sphere (Kageyama & Sato 2004).  A panel is the low-latitude
-- lon-lat rectangle theta_phys = 5π/24 + theta with
--   theta_phys in [π/4 - 2h, 3π/4 + 2h],  phi in [-3π/4 - 2h, 3π/4 + 2h],
-- h = π/48: the classical minimal panel extended by a 2-cell
-- interpolation margin.  Yin and Yang are
-- congruent under the involution (x,y,z) -> (-x,z,y), so this single
-- program is the kernel for BOTH panels: the check driver instantiates
-- the generated grid twice and, after every step, overwrites the
-- one-cell rim of each panel with bilinear interpolation from the
-- other panel -- the overset boundary condition.  The yaml walls are
-- mirror only as a placeholder; the rim cells they influence are
-- exactly the cells the driver overwrites.  The init below is the
-- global eigenmode Y_1^0 = cos(theta_global) in Yin coordinates
-- (theta_global = theta_phys on Yin).  The local phi origin is
-- phi0 = -19π/24, matching the check driver.  The
-- driver rewrites both panels with each of the three global l=1
-- Cartesian modes in turn, and checks their exact decay e^{-2t}.

dimension 3
axes θ, φ, z

param dt = 0.0003

embedding [ sin (5 * π / 24 + θ) * cos (φ - 19 * π / 24), sin (5 * π / 24 + θ) * sin (φ - 19 * π / 24), cos (5 * π / 24 + θ), z ]

field u : scalar @ primal

init:
  u := cos (5 * π / 24 + θ)

step:
  u' = u + dt * Δ u
The same physical Gaussian blob is seen by Yin (left) at its φ edge and by Yang (right) at its θ edge (the 2 panels are congruent under the involution (x,y,z)→(−x,z,y)). By t=0.18 the heat has flowed through the rim interpolation at the seam into the interior of Yang, and no discontinuity is visible at the panel boundary. The color scale is shared by both panels across all frames
The .fme is the kernel for one panel only (no compiler modification). The check driver holds 2 grid structs, swaps them into formura_data alternately, and after every step overwrites the 1-cell rim from the partner panel by bilinear interpolation. Verified: exact decay e−2t of the global l=1 eigenmodes x/y/z; panel-to-panel agreement; maximum principle.
